title: Serve Local HTML on Device
description: Build an HTML app in Gotcha chats and serve it on a local port via toybox netcat (Operator mode only).
instructions:
Purpose: When the user asks to build/develop/create an app, game, page, or tool and does not specify how to run it, make it immediately usable on this phone as a self-contained HTML page served on a local port. This is the smart default when local execution is possible. If the request is genuinely ambiguous (could be Android APK vs web app vs Python script vs Termux), ask one clarifying question: 'Do you want this runnable on this phone as a web app (HTML on a local port), or as an Android app / Python script / Termux program?' Then act on the answer — do not default to asking when the intent is clearly a web-playable game or page.
1. Write a single self-contained index.html (inline CSS+JS, CDN via https if needed, no local asset dependencies) to /storage/emulated/0/Gotcha/chats/<Slug>_<shortId>/index.html using write_file. Keep it under 100KB. This is the Gotcha world — do NOT use run_termux_command or Termux's $HOME for this file.
2. Pick a free port: try 8000, then 7777, 8080, 9000. Test with run_command: `toybox nc -z 127.0.0.1 8000 || echo free` — first free wins. Use timeout_seconds=5 for these probes.
3. Serve it with run_command (Operator mode only; Monitor cannot run this). Do NOT use run_termux_command for Gotcha-world files. Use a persistent loop with HTTP headers so every connection gets text/html:
   `nohup sh -c 'while true; do { printf "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8\r\nContent-Length: $(wc -c < "/storage/emulated/0/Gotcha/chats/<Slug>_<id>/index.html")\r\nCache-Control: no-cache\r\nAccess-Control-Allow-Origin: *\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"; cat "/storage/emulated/0/Gotcha/chats/<Slug>_<id>/index.html"; } | toybox nc -L -p <PORT> -q 1; done' > /data/local/tmp/serve_<PORT>.log 2>&1 & echo $!`
   If toybox nc -L is single-connection, the while-true loop keeps it alive for the browser and for a verification curl. If nohup is missing, fallback to `sh -c 'while true; do ...; done' &`.
4. Verify with run_command: `sleep 1; curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:<PORT> | head -n 20` must show HTTP/1.1 200 and Content-Type: text/html. Use timeout_seconds=5. If it fails, `ps | grep toybox` and retry with next free port.
5. Return to the user immediately: `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>` and `http://localhost:<PORT>` (both are secure contexts for camera/mic on Android Chrome) plus the file path. Do not wait for a follow-up 'run it at ...' message. Note: server lives until reboot or `pkill -f "toybox nc.*<PORT>"` via run_command.
6. If the user explicitly asked for Termux/Python/APK (e.g., 'run in Termux', 'make an APK'), do not force the web default — honor that and use the appropriate Termux/proot skill instead.
